english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}+y^{2}=1$ and let $H$ be the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{7}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$. Let $P(0,\lambda)$, where $\lambda>0$, be a point such that the pair of tangents drawn from $P$ to $E$ is the same pair of lines as the pair of tangents drawn from $P$ to $H$. Then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}+y^{2}=1$ है तथा $H$ अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{x^{2}}{7}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$ है। माना कि $P(0,\lambda)$, जहाँ $\lambda>0$, एक ऐसा बिन्दु है कि $P$ से $E$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखाओं का युग्म वही रेखा-युग्म है जो $P$ से $H$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखाओं का युग्म है। तब $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The $y$-terms already agree, so the pairs coincide iff $\dfrac{\lambda^{2}-1}{3}=\dfrac{\lambda^{2}+6}{7}\Rightarrow 4\lambda^{2}=25\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac52$
Check: tangents $y=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt7}{2}x+\dfrac52$; $3\cdot\dfrac74+1=\dfrac{25}{4}=7\cdot\dfrac74-6$, so they touch both curves
solution_full: The pair of tangents from $(x_{1},y_{1})$ to a conic $S=0$ is $SS_{1}=T^{2}$, where $S_{1}=S(x_{1},y_{1})$ and $T=0$ is the chord of contact form.

Both equations have the same coefficients of $y^{2}$, $y$ and the constant, so they represent the same pair of lines exactly when the $x^{2}$ coefficients agree: $\dfrac{\lambda^{2}-1}{3}=\dfrac{\lambda^{2}+6}{7}$.

Check by slopes: with $\lambda=\dfrac52$ the common joint equation is $\dfrac74x^{2}-y^{2}+5y-\dfrac{25}{4}=0$, i.e. $\dfrac74x^{2}=\left(y-\dfrac52\right)^{2}$, the lines $y=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt7}{2}x+\dfrac52$. For $E$: $a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}=3\cdot\dfrac74+1=\dfrac{25}{4}=c^{2}$. For $H$: $a^{2}m^{2}-b^{2}=7\cdot\dfrac74-6=\dfrac{25}{4}=c^{2}$, and $m^{2}=\dfrac74>\dfrac67$, so both lines touch $H$ at real points.

concept_use.Pair of tangents for Hyperbola: SS1 = T^2 for H from (0, lambda) gives (lambda^2+6)x^2/7 - y^2 + 2 lambda y - lambda^2 = 0.
concept_use.Pair of tangents for Ellipse: SS1 = T^2 for E from (0, lambda) gives (lambda^2-1)x^2/3 - y^2 + 2 lambda y - lambda^2 = 0; equating the two joint equations fixes lambda.

originality_note: New: the point is defined by the coincidence of two joint equations (the tangent pair to an ellipse and to a hyperbola from the same point), so the answer comes from comparing coefficients of two SS1 = T^2 equations (way 5). Closest known: equation of the pair of tangents from a point to an ellipse; common tangents of two conics. Different because: the condition is stated on the pairs from one point, and the joint equations turn out to share every coefficient except that of x^2.
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter introduced, conditions complete (quadrant / sign / branch stated), one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer equals the plan (positive decimal: 2.5). Changed: No change. Checked that lambda = 5/2 is the only positive value, that P is outside E (tangents real) and that both lines touch H at real points (m^2 = 7/4 > 6/7).
key_step: Write SS1 = T^2 for both conics from (0, lambda) and compare the joint equations.
justification: Two pair-of-tangents equations with a parameter must be expanded correctly and compared; the link (same pair of lines) is the idea, executed without options. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3) on common tangents of an ellipse and a parabola.
